column1: # experiment: E16 forward attention with FKL: the tensor-core DPP and the SIMT DPP against their unfused alternatives

column10: from `blocks` blocks of `calls_per_block` calls enqueued back to back between two CUDA events (the GPU time of the call
column11: no host gap between calls; the block lasts about E16_BLOCK_MS)
column12: after the warm-up; single_ms_median = median of `blocks` single calls
column13: each between two events and synchronised (launch latency included); TFLOP/s = 4 BH S^2 D (halved for causal) / time_ms_median; error against an fp32 attention of the same (dequantised) inputs for the first and the last head; kernels and per-kernel facts from capturing one call into a CUDA graph; the library chooses the tiles (no tuning); mma_epilogue_*: o * 1.25 + 0.5; SCHEDULES: mma_raw
column14: mma_epilogue_* and the K and V bf16 buffers of the *_unfused variants run the cp.async schedule with the library's raw-path tiles; the fused int8 and fp8 variants run the register-prefetch schedule with the library's non-raw tiles (a prologue cannot be applied inside a cp.async copy)
column15: so a fused-against-unfused prologue pair differs in load schedule and tiles as well as in fusion
column16: and is not a pure fusion effect; the epilogue pair runs the same kernel and schedule and differs only in the epilogue
